findings.premise: Explicit resolver context propagation and the specified serialization exclusions are sufficient to preserve session isolation and prevent persistence of temporary analysis data.

summary.prose: Temporary connections belong to a workbench session and a selected repository, so one-off files and other sources can be analyzed without saving connection configuration or credentials. Closing the panel or switching repositories preserves them; ending the workbench, losing its 90-second lease or restarting the daemon expires them. This story supplies the daemon session protocol and execution isolation; S005 supplies the lifetime explanation and manager UI.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a daemon-owned application service over the existing repository JSON registry and driver implementations. Separate saved commit, runtime activation and client refresh; use immutable credential generations and atomic JSON replacement rather than pretending the filesystem and keychain share a transaction. Temporary configurations remain in daemon memory under a workbench lease. All descriptions below are proposed architecture, not assertions of current implementation.

ownedContracts.purpose: Memory-only temporary state independent from panels and chat sessions.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface OpenConnectionSessionResult { sessionHandle: string; capability: string; daemonEpoch: string; heartbeatMs: 30000; leaseMs: 90000 } interface SessionResume { sessionHandle: string; capability: string; daemonEpoch: string } interface TemporaryConnectionStore { register(context: ConnectionAccessContext, request: MutationRequest): Promise<MutationOutcome>; end(sessionHandle: string): Promise<void> }

consumedContracts.name: Connection management protocol and driver descriptors

consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: type ConnectionScope = 'saved' | 'temporary'; interface ConnectionKey { repoRoot: string; scope: ConnectionScope; id: string } interface SafeConnection { key: ConnectionKey; revision: string; kind: string; family: 'rdbms'|'kv'|'file'; label?: string | undefined; publicConfig: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; declaredFamily?: string | undefined; registeredFamily?: string | undefined; effectiveFamily: string; compatibilityWarning?: string | undefined; credentialPresence: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>> } type CredentialPatch = { action: 'keep' } | { action: 'replace'; value: string } | { action: 'clear' }; interface DriverDescriptor { kind: string; family: 'rdbms'|'kv'|'file'; publicInputSchema: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>; secretSlots: readonly string[] } interface ManagementCapabilities { version: 2; daemonEpoch: string; features: readonly string[]; receiptRetentionDays: 30 }

consumedContracts.name: Revision-checked mutation and recovery outcomes
consumedContracts.purpose: Make persistence and retries truthful across registry and credential boundaries.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch: interface OperationTicket { operationId: string; lookupRoot: string; scope: ConnectionScope; connectionId: string; mode: "create"|"update"|"remove"; issuedAt: string; expiresAt: string; signature: string } interface OperationStatusRequest { ticket: OperationTicket } interface MutationRequest { ticket: OperationTicket; operationId: string; key: ConnectionKey; mode: 'create'|'update'|'remove'; expectedRevision?: string | undefined; publicPatch?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> | undefined; credentials?: Readonly<Record<string, CredentialPatch>> | undefined } type ManagementErrorCode = 'invalid-input'|'duplicate-id'|'conflict'|'not-found'|'busy'|'registry-unreadable'|'secret-unavailable'|'recovery-required'|'session-expired'|'upgrade-required'|'operation-mismatch'|'reconciliation-required'; interface CommittedOutcome { operationId: string; revision: string; registration: 'persisted'|'session-added'|'removed'; activation: 'active'|'pending'|'failed'|'not-applicable'; credentialCleanup: 'complete'|'pending' } type MutationOutcome = { status: 'committed'; value: CommittedOutcome } | { status: 'rejected'; code: ManagementErrorCode; message: string }; type OperationStatus = { status:'committed'; value:CommittedOutcome } | { status:'pending'|'not-seen'|'reconciliation-required' }; interface ActivationRetry { key: ConnectionKey; committedRevision: string }

consumedContracts.name: Memory-only file execution and conversion policy
consumedContracts.purpose: A shared file-driver foundation for transient tests and temporary sessions without reversing branch dependencies.

boundary.internal: Session open/resume/heartbeat/end, memory-only temporary overlays and receipts, trusted execution-context propagation through analyzer/tool/MCP call paths, expiry and saved/temporary collision rules. Bind the S001-owned sc8 file execution policy to session identity and expiry; S001 owns conversion, cache-policy isolation and private DuckDB lifecycle. Every native/converted kind uses that foundation rather than a branch-local converter.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Safe saved-config read/patch, canonical repo validation, driver profiles, registry metadata/receipts and crash recovery, immutable secret generation staging, compatibility adapters and lease accounting foundation. Does not own temporary storage or rich manager layout. Preserve saved-only scope-local lookup and legacy pinned-family values; signed operation tickets make expiry/replay decidable after receipt pruning. Own the shared memory-only conversion/probe driver foundation, converter-cache policy/identity changes and private DuckDB lifecycle (sc8), completed before the S002/S003 branches.
Transient process probe transport, deadline/cancellation and sanitization. Uses foundational context slots without depending on s3’s session implementation.
Removal coordination for both scopes, busy/revision enforcement, confirmation state, postcommit credential cleanup retry and operation-status recovery. Never invokes source data deletion.

Settings contributions and shared command routing, themed editor/forms, filters, dirty guards, stale-test suppression and truthful feedback in extension and external IDE. HLD has inspected the external pane, actions, service, mirrored types and Settings registrations; S005 implements the recorded plan and validates its mirrored contract before integration acceptance.

nonFunctional.performance: Draft tests have a 10-second parent-enforced deadline, with forced child reap if graceful termination fails. Workbench heartbeat is 30 seconds and expiry 90 seconds after last valid heartbeat. Mutations serialize per repo; list/filter work does not perform driver probes. LLD load tests must verify no leaked children, leases or session entries after cancellation/expiry.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns every saved/temporary config and credential decision; client labels/PIDs are not authorization. Registered-root eligibility gates management and temporary operations; saved-only analysis preserves canonical scope-local lookup without gaining mutation rights. Safe read responses return a profile allowlist and presence booleans only. Secrets, capabilities and full requests never enter logs, receipts, prompts, artifacts, telemetry or checkpoints. Temporary inputs never reach disk or keychain. A test worker receives config via private IPC and may not emit raw driver errors. Temporary file conversion, query spill and metadata/logging are part of the no-persistence boundary, including test workers.
nonFunctional.observability: Use getLogger with operation ID, safe code, repo ID, scope, revision and phase only; timing and counters for commit, activation, recovery, timeout, busy refusal and session expiry. No raw exceptions or endpoint/options. Operation status exposes committed truth even when response delivery or activation failed. Recovery-required and cleanup-pending are visible and actionable.
nonFunctional.durability: Saved JSON remains authoritative. Same-directory atomic rename/fsync commits registry, revisions and receipts together; immutable keychain generations preserve previous effective credentials until commit. Recover preparation records before enabling mutation. Issue signed 30-day operation tickets; preserve receipts through ticket expiry and pending cleanup, and distinguish expired-unreceipted from valid-not-seen after restart. Temporary state and receipts expire on explicit session end, 90-second lease loss or daemon epoch change.

api.name: TemporaryConnectionStore
api.signature: interface TemporaryConnectionStore { open(context: TrustedRpcContext, request: { repoRoot: string }): Promise<OpenConnectionSessionResult>; resume(context: TrustedRpcContext, request: SessionResume): Promise<OpenConnectionSessionResult>; heartbeat(context: TrustedRpcContext): Promise<{ status: 'active'; leaseMs: 90000 }>; register(context: ConnectionAccessContext, request: MutationRequest): Promise<MutationOutcome>; end(sessionHandle: string): Promise<void>; }

parameters.name: context
parameters.purpose: Daemon-minted transport identity or derived validated access, never client-deserialized authority.

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: Strict session bootstrap/resume or existing revision-checked mutation input; capability accepted only on dedicated session control/attach endpoint.

parameters.name: sessionHandle
parameters.purpose: Internal owner lifecycle identifier; wire end first validates transport attachment and can end only its bound session.

returns.meaning: Session handle and capability returned only at authenticated bootstrap/resume; temporary mutation uses session-added commit truth and separate activation outcome.

errors.condition: Wrong epoch, missing/invalid capability, unattached execution context or ended/expired session.
Malformed/excess-size input or noncanonical/unregistered management root.
Existing contract rules for collisions, revisions, active use, nonidentical retries and expired/unverifiable tickets.

preconditions: sc5 methods are proposed additions, not existing support. Use a fixed private RPC family db.connections.v2.session.open/resume/attach/heartbeat/end. End by handle is an internal function; public end accepts no arbitrary handle and derives it from the authenticated transport.

Open creates a random256-bit handle, separate random256-bit bearer capability and random session-memory HMAC key; only capability digest is retained for constant-time verification. Dedicated control transport attachment survives transient reconnect through resume; data/MCP transports use attach and cannot renew the lease.

Canonical registered-root eligibility is required for each temporary management operation and overlay. One session may own overlays for multiple eligible roots; panel/repo switch never ends it. No authorization from PID/client label/chat ID.
Session methods and all session-bound data work route to main daemon, not worker-thread stores. A daemon-owned immutable access context is bound to request lifetime and validated again after awaits.
postconditions: Open/resume returns heartbeatMs30000/leaseMs90000. Heartbeat is accepted only on current control generation; resume atomically increments generation and detaches the old control transport. An exactly-at-deadline request expires before authorization; only a valid pre-deadline heartbeat extends the monotonic deadline.

Temporary create/update/status/ticket/read/list/activation bind existing sc1/sc2 keys and schema; ticket signature binds session via its private memory key, request HMAC covers full canonical payload, and receipts contain only safe outcomes. Same-ID changed-payload replay rejects. Session expiry invalidates all tickets/receipts regardless of wall clock.

register resolves Keep only from selected immutable in-memory generation; Replace/Clear update private data only. Never call resolveConfigSecrets/keychain/list/load/adoption or any registry writer for temporary state. Paths use existing prepareRuntimeConfig. New ID/kind/family immutable per existing profile rules.

Create/update commits memory entry + revision + receipt atomically under the same root gate as saved ID reservation. Activation is afterward; failure does not erase committed truth. Existing active leases refuse update; no user remove workflow in S003.

End/lease expiry first closes admission and detaches every transport; cancels owned runs/probes/conversion and synchronously prevents further resolution; drops capabilities/receipts/config secret references, then awaits active operations and owned close. Failures leave a closed cleanup record with only owned runtime handles and safe counters; no success reported while a child/resource remains. Daemon shutdown awaits drains; process restart has no recoverable temporary state.

Limit64 live sessions,64 connections/session,8MiB cumulative serialized config/session and16384 receipts/session; return existing busy on quota before committing, never evict live receipts silently. Per temporary file resource uses existing sc8 memoryBudgetBytes256MiB/allowSpillfalse; file source/data/config/capability material never goes to temp/cache/logs. Budgets are fixed internal limits, not a UI option. JS garbage collection limits mean logical erasure rather than guaranteed physical zeroization.

api.name: createConnectionResolver

parameters.name: ports
parameters.purpose: Install the sc5 memory owner as existing sessionOverlay provider while retaining saved pool source.

returns.meaning: Saved-only resolution when context has no session; otherwise saved plus only the validated session overlay matching exact canonical lookupRoot.

errors.condition: Presented session context is stale/wrong-owner/wrong-root; do not retry through saved-only fallback.
Any unexpected overlap between saved and visible temporary entries; resolution must not silently shadow.

preconditions: Consume sc3 without redefining leases or saved root semantics. Context comes from validated transport/execution carrier, never serialized analyzer focus/plan/tool args.

Saved reservation must reject an ID held in any active overlay at that root, including another workbench; temporary create rejects saved IDs but same temporary ID may exist in different isolated sessions. One root-serialized coordinator performs both checks and commit while holding the shared root gate.

Unattached CLI/MCP and scope-local unregistered/nested saved lookup remain saved-only exactly as before; temporary lookup requires matching eligible root. Context with a session but incompatible root must reject session-expired, never attach a nearby root.
postconditions: Session overlay returns safe projection only; credentials and HMAC/capability never leave owner. Every list/lease/withConnection revalidates state; no global current session or ambient AsyncLocalStorage persisted state.

All current data consumers receive explicit immutable access context via ToolDeps and analyzer runtime/exploration/measure context. Request/run registry holds owner/run IDs and cancellation only in daemon memory. Wire thread projection has no capability; session work stays main-daemon and no handle/capability enters checkpoint/telemetry/prompt/artifact serialization.

MCP child initial capability arrives on a private inherited control pipe, never argv/settings/config/log; child attaches its RPC data transport then discards raw bootstrap buffer and clears environment fallback. Unattached MCP remains saved-only. Reconnect requires explicit resume; an old run with lost temporary context rejects session-expired instead of saved fallback.

Session lifetime cancellation is registered through S002 RequestLifetime drains and propagated through full analyzer/tool driver callback lifetime. Existing callback leases prevent premature release; do not reconstruct lease counters in consumers.

Session-bound stream uses RequestLifetime completion/seal/drain in finally even on send failure. Router activity/maintenance hold lasts through stream completion AND owned drain. Owner abort affects only bound work.

StepToolRunner gains an optional fourth internal context argument; StepCallContext gains readonly connectionAccess/executionPolicy fields set by the host.

forwardStep attaches EVERY fresh socket before step.call. No bootstrap capability in rawArgs, serialized caller context or environment. Attach acknowledgement must match current daemon epoch; failure rejects instead of dispatching saved-only.

Session-authenticated routing is decided before worker selection for stream/unary traffic. Only session management/safe metadata, draft probes, read-only db tools and analyze calls are admitted in session-memory mode. Session-bound workflow/build/review/tracker or other unclassified persistence-capable methods return upgrade-required before executing; they are not silently downgraded.

Any session-bound persisted run/status/continuation lookup validates owner BEFORE loading outputs. Owner-derived memory policy remains sticky through one-shot, multi-turn, nested task and provider calls; missing policy/binding fails closed.

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed daemon-memory aggregate: random handle, capability digest, epoch, monotonic leaseDeadline, current control identity/generation, authenticated data attachments, per-root overlays, memory signing key and owned run cancellations. Direction/cardinality: session owns0..many repo overlays and transport attachments; overlay belongs exactly1 session and1 canonical root; session owns no saved pool. Logical ACTIVE→CLOSING→CLOSED state is irreversible. Reconnect can rebind while active, never revive expired session. Unfinished cleanup retains only closed resource handles, not retrievable configs/credentials. No session data is stored in DB/JSON/keychain.

Each (session,canonical root,id) owns one current immutable config/credential generation and revision plus active callback leases, construction/close promise and memory-only file execution resource. Different sessions may reuse IDs without sharing drivers/tables. Shared root mutation gate excludes saved-vs-temporary ID races; saved creates query all active reservations. Existing saved registry generation and unknown fields untouched. Config/read responses go through driver-profile safe allowlist; parent memory-only runtime construction bypasses keychain. Dynamic logs never contain source/options/URL/secrets; SDK logging policy must also be quiet for temporary operations.

Session+repo+operation ID indexes canonical keyed request HMAC and sc2 safe committed outcome; no plaintext patch or credentials. Receipt belongs exactly1 session and1 overlay/root; multiple receipts may refer to an entry revision. TicketexpiresAt=min(now+90000ms,current signed lease expiry); heartbeat extends session life but not previously issued tickets. Committed receipt remains queryable for entire session, even expired ticket; expired ticket with no receipt returns reconciliation-required; epoch/session loss always session-expired. Concurrent same-ID calls share in-flight result. Capacity refuses new ticket/commit before state change rather than discarding live history.

No sc3 wire shape change: optional sessionHandle is only a daemon-validated authority reference. Add an out-of-band execution-context carrier to ToolDeps, analyzer runtime/exploration/measure and MCP handler lifetimes. No raw capability/session metadata in prompt/tool args/analyze opaque state/checkpoint/artifacts. Maintain daemon-memory continuation binding so a temporary run whose process/context is lost fails explicitly rather than reconstructing saved-only authority. Saved-only consumers still use their exact own-directory lookupRoot; attach never grants management eligibility.

Review correction: all session-attached execution is conservatively session-memory, including saved-only steps within that execution and every dependent plan/report/error result. This is a daemon-derived sticky policy, never an input flag. Validate active owner/root and every previously used connection revision before executing, serving prior state or consulting any memory result. First admission forbids all shared/persistent cache reads AND writes; there is no cross-call memory result cache in this design. Existing opaque continuation results remain only in session-owned memory and are invalidated on any used revision change, session end or epoch loss. A revision change returns conflict/restart guidance rather than reusing stale outputs. Scope selection is validated before any cache optimization. [[c12]]

No getCachedExploration/putCachedExploration for either executePlan or stepPlan, including narrow resume, parameter substitution and dependency outputs. No readBundle/writeBundle, shaper tool-result dump, planner attempt/feedback/final plan, task record, orchestrator run record, analyze trace, chat/tool history, artifact/checkpoint, LMDB/Lance or telemetry output containing session-derived input/output is read/written by a session-memory run. There is no output persistence followed by cleanup: writes are prevented before the sink. Existing saved-only calls retain existing caching. A future caller that cannot propagate the sticky policy must reject before executing a temporary operation; a persisted record may contain no reusable session authority or output. [[c12]]

S003 also routes session-derived provider requests only through a provider mode whose local history/cache/trace behavior has been proven nonpersistent; a provider/CLI path that cannot meet this boundary returns unsupported-temporary before sending source data. No cloud SDK or direct REST provider is added. Configs/secrets/capabilities never enter prompts regardless of provider. Normal saved runs retain their behavior. Resource budget is the production sc8 default256MiB, not the test helper's64MiB override. [[c13]]

Proposed additive internal carrier (not a wire schema): readonly connectionAccess?: ConnectionAccessContext; readonly executionPolicy?: { readonly mode: 'saved' | 'session-memory'; readonly bindingId: string }; bindingId is an opaque daemon-memory owner/run lookup, never trusted from params and never persisted. ShapeOpts/RunShaperArgs, ExecutePlanArgs, ExplorationRunnerContext, TemplateExecuteArgs, RunExecutorArgs, ToolDeps and StepCallContext inherit the same carrier. Any session-memory call without a live binding fails session-expired. Main-daemon owner records hold cancellation/drain and used-revision vector; callbacks pass the carrier explicitly, not a global mutable current session.

Concrete migration inventory (proposed changes; existing behavior established by supplemental analyzer plus direct reads and the current TypeScript-resolved source inventory). Rows grouping files require the named proving test to exercise EACH listed site and every runtime branch, not just a helper. [[c12]] [[c14]]

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Implement the chosen memory owner, authenticated control/data attachment lifecycle, heartbeat/expiry, overlay+receipt identity, cancellation/drain and explicit sc5 integration ports consumed by S004/S005.

Strict additive session RPC methods; use existing connection key/scope/schema, safe descriptor/projection and error codes. Capabilities advertise session support only after existing release gate and session propagation evidence; no v2 method silently changes legacy return shapes.

Reuse MutationRequest, signed OperationTicket shape, safe MutationOutcome and canonical request HMAC primitives with session-local ephemeral key/receipts. Existing saved coordinator gains only an active-ID reservation callback under its root gate; no saved commit/recovery redesign.

Use sessionOverlay and callback lease contract; propagate trusted context additively to all inventoried consumers, and invalidate on owner expiry. Export an internal drain/lease port to S004 without implementing removal UI/coordination.

Use existing memory-only execution/conversion at root/session/id/revision identity,256MiB/resource,allowSpillfalse. All native and converted readers use shared implementation; if absent/overbudget reject explicitly before persistent writes. No converter redesign.

errorCases.detection: Strict bounded decoder rejects extra fields; constant-time digest comparison, current control generation, daemon epoch and monotonic active-state checks fail before lookup or credential access.
errorCases.response: Fixed session-expired; zero driver creation/registry/keychain access; never fallback to saved or log the rejected token.
errorCases.userImpact: Reconnect with still-live private capability or re-add temporary connections after expiry.

errorCases.scenario: Root is unregistered, canonical mismatch or overlay belongs to another lookupRoot
errorCases.detection: realpath+registered-root eligibility check and exact overlay root comparison run at admission and after awaits.
errorCases.response: invalid-input for malformed/unregistered management root; session-expired for unauthorized attachment/root context. Saved-only scope-local reads remain unchanged.
errorCases.userImpact: Select the intended registered repository; saved sources can still be read through the legacy lane.

errorCases.scenario: Saved/temporary creation races or update during full-use lease
errorCases.detection: Inside existing root mutation coordinator check saved IDs and all live overlay reservations atomically with commit; verify expected revision and foundational active/barrier counts.
errorCases.response: duplicate-id, conflict or busy with no partial memory commit or persistent changes.
errorCases.userImpact: Choose another ID or retry after current use; never silently replace/shadow a source.

errorCases.scenario: Lost response or changed payload reuses operation ID
errorCases.detection: Session-memory ticket signature/epoch/root/key/mode/expiry checks and canonical payload HMAC compare against in-flight/receipt entry.
errorCases.response: Identical replay/status returns same committed result; changed body operation-mismatch. Expired ticket with no receipt reconciliation-required. Missing session always session-expired, not not-seen.
errorCases.userImpact: Client can distinguish committed addition from a retry that must not happen.

errorCases.scenario: Expiry/end races with preparation, construction, activation, callback or temporary draft probe
errorCases.detection: Registry marks CLOSING synchronously, invalidates attachments/entry generation, aborts run signals, and checks generation after every awaited operation before publication.
errorCases.response: Reject new work session-expired; late built resources immediately enter owned close; no late entry resurrection. Preserve safe already-committed receipt only while session remains active. End acknowledges only after drain; transport lifetime retains cleanup even if response disappears.
errorCases.userImpact: Current temporary operation is canceled; re-add in a new session when needed.

errorCases.scenario: Temporary runtime, conversion or disposal fails
errorCases.detection: Owned construction/probe/close promises reject; sc8 reports unsupported-temporary/resource-limit before persistence, and parent counters detect non-drained resources.
errorCases.response: Safe fixed activation failed/pending outcome after memory commit; no false rollback or source deletion. CLOSING remains inaccessible and retains retryable cleanup handles/counters; close failure is not swallowed. Reuse S002 force-reap only for its own probe children, never arbitrary PIDs.
errorCases.userImpact: Row may be session-added but activation failed; safe guidance permits revision-scoped activation retry. End may report pending cleanup without reviving the row.

errorCases.scenario: Quota exhaustion or attempt to persist temporary authority/config
errorCases.detection: Admission compares fixed memory/session/receipt limits before commit; production serialization inventory and allowlists reject sessionHandle/capability/effective config in durable request/run artifacts and telemetry.
errorCases.response: busy without evicting live state; deny persistence path and return fixed safe failure. Drop raw SDK errors and suppress credential/source-bearing logs.
errorCases.userImpact: User can end unused sessions or use saved scope deliberately; no automatic save/cache fallback.

errorCases.scenario: Persistent cache hit or continuation attempts to bypass owner resolution
errorCases.detection: At run admission and before any prior-output reuse, validate live daemon binding and used-revision vector. Sticky session-memory policy prevents every shared cache read/write, including error/retry branches; spy tests check sink calls, not only final files.
errorCases.response: No persistent read/write; recompute under current owner. Revision change yields conflict; owner loss yields session-expired. Never trust a cached same-ID saved result. Reject unsupported persistence-capable methods/providers before executing.
errorCases.userImpact: Temporary results stay isolated; caller restarts stale work instead of seeing another session data.

edgeCases.input: Same temporary ID in sessions A and B at the same root
edgeCases.expected: Allowed; separate immutable generations, credentials, resources, receipts and leases. Saved create with that ID is blocked until both reservations are gone.

edgeCases.input: Panel close or repository A→B→A switch
edgeCases.expected: No lifecycle event; same session retains both root overlays. Only current exact-root access resolves each overlay; control heartbeats continue independently.

edgeCases.input: Control disconnect followed by resume within90seconds
edgeCases.expected: Data remains in memory; resume with same capability/epoch transfers control generation. Old control heartbeat/end cannot affect new generation. A disconnected data request cancels only its owned work, not the whole session.

edgeCases.input: Heartbeat arrives exactly at deadline or wall clock moves
edgeCases.expected: Expire before authenticating at >=monotonic deadline. Wall-clock ticket time remains bounded by signed issued expiry; it never authorizes an expired monotonic session.

edgeCases.input: Unattached CLI/MCP or legacy directory-scoped saved analysis
edgeCases.expected: Saved-only lookup with exact original scope root, including unregistered/nested saved registries. No implicit management eligibility or auto-created session.

edgeCases.input: An analysis continuation/checkpoint survives daemon epoch change
edgeCases.expected: Continuation with temporary-use marker requires a live daemon-memory binding; if absent reject session-expired with re-add guidance. Never reconstruct temporary authority from checkpoint or reuse same-named saved source.

edgeCases.input: Header-only file or unavailable Arrow/Feather reader
edgeCases.expected: Retain sc8 truth: valid empty input may succeed; missing local reader reports unsupported-temporary before any INSTALL/temp/cache write. S003 does not silently enable absent readers.

edgeCases.input: Capability-gated release still disabled or mixed-version client
edgeCases.expected: No temporary features advertised and no session mutation admitted. Existing saved reads remain available; return upgrade-required for unsupported session methods.

invariantsToPreserve.text: sc1/sc3 safe keys/access and callback leases remain authoritative; discovery bundle symbol.locate and manual pool-cache read establish current signatures.
Legacy repo-pool registerEphemeral must not become a user session store; usage.example graph was incomplete and manual inventory confirms the existing definition only.
Server-minted identity/epoch and main-daemon request lifetime remain unforgeable; consume S002 prepareTemporary and private worker lifecycle rather than redesign it.
Existing resolver/owned-file/context tests stay regression gates; session work extends them with actual production wiring and zero-persistence evidence.

migration.stateBefore: S1 bundles symbol.locate and search.text plus manual src/daemon/db/pool-cache.ts reads establish a saved resolver with fail-closed optional sessionOverlay; src/analyze/connection-access.ts and toolAccess in src/daemon/tools/builtins/db/index.ts currently construct saved-only contexts. The repo pool has registerEphemeral but no demonstrated workbench session owner. S002 BUILD is approved with MSSQL actual-service coverage pending and one full-sweep warning; S001 review is deferred, and the shipped gate is disabled.
migration.stateAfter: Proposed: sc5 memory owner and strict session lifecycle methods supply isolated per-session/per-root temporary entries, receipts and resources through existing sc3 resolver hooks. Every inventoried analyzer/tool/MCP consumer carries daemon-validated context out of band; legacy/unattached saved-only paths keep their current lookup rules. No JSON/keychain/graph/vector migration, saved registry rewrite or existing connection adoption.

migrationSteps.action: Add additive bounded session protocol and daemon-memory owner behind disabled existing capability gate; keep saved APIs and all persisted formats unchanged. Add root coordinator reservation hook as a consumer of saved coordinator; no automatic registry adoption.
prerequisiteFlags: existing connection management gate remains disabled

migrationSteps.action: Install owner lifecycle and overlay resolver hooks with memory-only credentials/resources. Add attach/control generation and shutdown drain, leaving user remove and UI to S004/S005. Build isolated real-IPC tests before any capability advertisement.

Propagate explicit trusted context through the complete analyzer/tool/MCP inventory and private bootstrap pipe. Keep session-bound calls main-daemon; attach no capability to serialized state and reject lost temporary continuations. Regenerate inventory as callers move; no production site left unclassified.

Run each task's relevant suite, then final build/full sweep after all tasks. Review source/compiled gate evidence and exact no-persistence/cancellation tests. Keep feature disabled until foundation review, session inventory and both client integration prerequisites are independently verified; do not treat pending SQL Server coverage as green.
prerequisiteFlags: independent S001 review and foundation gates
S005 client integration evidence before user release

migrationSteps.action: On deliberate rollback disable session advertisement/admission first, expire and drain only owned temporary sessions/resources, then remove overlay/context wiring. Communicate temporary session loss as the documented ephemeral lifetime; saved registrations and keychain data are untouched. No live restart is part of design validation.

migration.backwardCompat: All session protocol changes are additive; legacy list/save/test return shapes and S001 safe-read/profiles remain. Missing session context means saved-only only for a genuinely unattached new request. A request/continuation known to have used temporary state rejects if its binding is absent, with no same-name saved fallback. Exact nested/unregistered directory saved lookups and pinned legacy families are regression gates. Rollback intentionally loses ephemeral sessions, not saved data; old daemon/client combinations get upgrade-required rather than a fake empty list.

alternativesConsidered.name: Session registry with owned in-memory entries
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One daemon session registry owns separate per-repository overlays of immutable temporary entries.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Smallest complete sc5 shape: daemon issues workbench handle/capability and keeps a memory-only session record with repo overlays, credentials and receipts. Each overlay implements the existing ConnectionResolver callback contract using the foundational lease gate, driver factories, materializeDraft and sc8 memory-only resource policy; it never registers into the saved pool. Trusted transport attachment and an explicit execution-context carrier provide access without changing wire MutationRequest/ConnectionKey semantics. Saved ID reservation and temporary commit share the existing per-root mutation coordinator. S004 consumes an internal lifecycle/removal port and S005 consumes the session protocol; no UI, converter or saved persistence redesign.
pros: Strong ownership and exact memory-only boundary with no saved loader/keychain paths in temporary construction.
Fits existing sessionOverlay resolver injection and S002 prepareTemporary hook.
Minimum new state: session, repo overlay, entry, receipt and active-use records.
cons: Must implement temporary entry lifecycle over existing lease primitives rather than reusing every DriverPool internal.
Requires complete consumer/context propagation inventory; incomplete graph alone is insufficient.

alternativesConsidered.name: One injected DriverPool per session and repository
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each overlay delegates runtime entries to a pool whose configuration and secret providers are entirely in memory.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the same sc5 session/capability protocol and sc1/sc2/sc3/sc8 contracts, but add explicit configuration-source and credential-source ports to DriverPool; instantiate one isolated temporary pool per session/repository. The saved default providers retain existing behavior, while the temporary providers have no disk/keychain capability. Memory-only policy identity uses session/repo/revision and session end closes the owned pool. Registry/tickets/receipts remain in the sc5 memory owner. This is an additive integration at the S001 pool port, requiring owner compatibility review rather than redesign of saved contracts.
pros: Reuses current pool construction/idle-close and callback lease mechanics.
Single familiar runtime abstraction for saved and temporary drivers.
cons: Broader changes to S001-owned pool internals and stronger proof against accidental reload/secret fallback required.
Current pool build calls saved secret resolution and reload paths, so injecting only a factory would be insufficient.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Protocol is compatible, but memory-only and lifecycle safety depend on broader changes to saved-pool internals; not the smallest complete integration.

erDefinition.narrative: Shows the proposed in-memory ownership boundary. Sessions own repository overlays and receipts; overlays own entries and resources. Saved pools remain separate and only meet the overlay at the validated resolver.

WorkbenchConnectionSession.description: One daemon-epoch workbench lifetime; capability digest and signing key remain in memory.

handle.description: Opaque random session identifier, never persisted.

overlays.description: Zero or more repository overlays exclusively owned by this session.

attachments.description: Control and data transports authenticated to this session.

RepositoryOverlay.description: Exactly one session and one canonical registered root; no saved registry ownership.

entries.description: Temporary connection generations owned by this session/root.

receipts.description: Safe memory-only mutation outcomes retained through session lifetime.

TemporaryEntry.description: One isolated temporary ID/revision and private credentials; owns runtime resource.

resource.description: At most one constructed owned driver/private file resource for current generation.

TemporaryReceipt.description: One session/root operation result and request HMAC; never contains plaintext credentials.

TransportAttachment.description: Validated current control generation or data attachment; no authority from client labels.

RuntimeResource.description: Private driver/lease boundary; never shared with saved pool or another session.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: Proposed ordering across trusted control/data transports, session ownership, root mutation arbitration and leased resources. The admission barrier precedes cancellation and drain so expiry cannot publish late resources or silently resolve saved sources.

participants.label: Workbench control channel
participants.description: Private in-memory capability holder, independent of panels and chat IDs.

participants.label: Daemon session owner
participants.description: Validates capability/epoch/generation and monotonic lease; owns memory-only overlays.

participants.label: Shared root coordinator
participants.description: Serializes saved/temporary reservations and revision changes.

participants.label: Attached analyzer/tool/MCP request
participants.description: Carries daemon-validated access out of band; never stores capability in request artifacts.

participants.label: Context-bound resolver
participants.description: Combines exact-root saved read with this session overlay after validation.

participants.label: Owned driver/sc8 resource
participants.description: Callback leases cover full use; file resource is private and memory-only.

messages.label: Open at registered canonical root
messages.description: Daemon mints session handle, capability and ephemeral signing key.

messages.label: Private bootstrap: epoch, handle, capability; heartbeat30s/lease90s
messages.description: Only private control channel receives credentials; no persistence/logging.

messages.label: Attach with private bootstrap capability
messages.description: Authenticate data transport to session without granting control heartbeat/end rights.

messages.label: Install sticky session-memory execution policy
messages.description: Before cache lookup, disable persistent exploration/bundle/planner/task/run/history/trace reads and writes for the whole session-bound run.

messages.label: Create/update temporary draft with signed ticket
messages.description: Strict sc1/sc2 request materializes owned memory credentials.

messages.label: Check saved IDs, live reservations, expected revision and busy use
messages.description: Same root gate used by saved create; collision cannot race.

messages.label: Commit memory entry/revision/receipt atomically
messages.description: No JSON/keychain/journal write; activation remains separate.

messages.label: Resolve exact lookupRoot with validated session context
messages.description: Missing/stale temporary binding fails, never falls back to a same-named saved source.

messages.label: Validate active binding and prior revision vector
messages.description: Before any continuation result reuse, reject expired/wrong-owner/stale revision; never return a warm saved or other-session cache hit.

messages.label: Run full callback under revision lease
messages.description: Reuse sc3 lease accounting and sc8 session/root/id/revision resource identity.

messages.label: Explicit end, or owner detects90s heartbeat loss
messages.description: At deadline owner first marks CLOSING and rejects admission; panel close/root switch does not send end.

messages.label: Invalidate attachments and abort owned runs/probes
messages.description: Retain request drain until actual process and callback cleanup finish.

messages.label: Reject all new session resolution
messages.description: Root reservations remain until required in-flight construction/use is no longer publishable.

messages.label: Drain callback, cancel conversion and close owned resources
messages.description: No source file deletion or unrelated PID signaling.

messages.label: Owned close/reap completes or safe cleanup-pending
messages.description: Only successful drain permits completed end acknowledgement; failures keep inaccessible cleanup state.

messages.label: End complete after drain; memory references removed
messages.description: No temporary state survives daemon epoch restart; logical erasure does not promise physical JS heap zeroization.
